fixes.explanation: Not even close, friend. The singer says, "My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD…" (Psalm 84:2). That is not a man checking his watch and saying he's in no hurry. Fainting is a whole other level of wanting.
Ha, a swallow with a treasure chest. I would pay to see that. But the verse says she places her young near the altars (Psalm 84:3). Treasures never come up in that line, only her little ones.

Yes, friend. "Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage." (Psalm 84:5). Their strength isn't packed in their bags. It's in the LORD, and that's a good thing to carry on a long road.

Right, friend. "They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion." (Psalm 84:7). They don't turn back. Each one makes it to Zion and appears before God, with no U-turns on this road.
Yes, friend! "For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere." (Psalm 84:10). One day against a thousand, and the one day wins. That's some math I can get behind.

Not quite, friend. The singer says, "For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere." (Psalm 84:10). One day there is better than a thousand days anywhere else. That's a lot more than just the same.

Right, friend. The singer says, "I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked." (Psalm 84:10). A doorkeeper is the one at the entrance of God's house. That's the place he says he would rather be.
